arjun: Heads up — starting coordination for the private metrics exporter project. Need a handshake spec for on-prem agents, firewall allowlist, KMS signing/audit hooks, and console quotas/dashboard inputs. Who's available to discuss tradeoffs? jess: on it. do we have a preferred flow: agent-pull vs agent-push? pull seems safer (no inbound ports) but adds polling. laura: +1 for pull with mTLS client auth. Agent initiates outbound TLS to our collector endpoint, presents client cert. This avoids opening inbound ports on customer infra. For VPC customers we can provide a VPC endpoint + private link. mike: mTLS is fine, but air-gapped customers are a pain. We should also support an upload-relay option (customer uploads tarball to an S3-like bucket we poll) or a relay appliance they run that forwards to us. arjun: KMS requirement from compliance: customers want audit entries for every key usage during exporter registration and key wrapping. We need an audit hook that logs 'exporter-registration' events to the customer's audit stream. @infra-bot can we wire that? infra-bot: infra-bot: created INF-827 "KMS audit hook for exporter registration" and linked to key-usage-logs. Assigned to @mike. CI job will validate audit delivery. jess: :eyes: UX note — console should show per-exporter quotas (eg throughput rps, token budget), onboarding checklist (firewall hostnames, cert rotation), and estimated egress cost. That'll reduce support questions. prod-ops: For rollouts: suggest canary at the customer org level + metric sampling toggles. Also routing: support dual-write to primary + fallback for safe migrations. Canary groups and sampling config need to be plumbed into the registration response. laura: Proposed internal API: POST /v1/exporters/register -> returns {credentials, allowed_hosts, policy_id, routing_mode}. Debate: gRPC streaming vs REST+WebSocket. Runtime team likes gRPC for TLS+streaming, product prefers REST for proxy compatibility. mike: gRPC is great but enterprise proxies often kill it. REST + WebSockets gives streaming semantics without gRPC framing issues. Also simpler for customers to debug. arjun: Good point — keep both on the roadmap, ship REST+WebSocket first. Also make the registration response include: allowed_outbound_hosts (list of hostnames), required_ports (usually 443), and kms_audit_event_id. jess: I'll mock a console wireframe showing: exporter status, last handshake time, cert expiry, quota usage, and a firewall checklist (hosts + sample ip ranges). laura: I'll draft the handshake spec and include a minimal cURL example + cert rotation snippet. Example: ```bash curl --cert client.pem --key client.key \ -X POST https://metrics.redwood-internal.net/v1/exporters/register \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"org_id":"org-123","agent_id":"agent-42"}' ``` and rotation note: rotate client certs via POST /v1/exporters/{id}/rotate and emit kms.audit event. mike: Firewall docs note: outbound 443 only. hostnames: metrics.redwood-internal.net, kms.redwood-internal.net, and optional relay.
For VPC customers, include the private endpoint FQDN to allow SRV/DNS entries. arjun: Action items: 1) eng-runtime (laura) draft handshake spec (REST+WS first; gRPC followup) 2) eng-infra (mike) doc firewall hostnames + KMS audit hooks 3) product (jess) console quota & onboarding wireframe 4) prod-ops (prod-ops) define canary groups and routing policy schema. Sync Thu 10:00am PT. :thumbsup: jess: +1, will have a mock by Wed EOD. laura: I'll include a short section on cert rotation and sample logs to ship to the audit pipeline. deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created epic ENG-telemetry-exporters and linked INF-827 and PRD-430. arjun: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll capture the spec in the ENG RFC and iterate in the sync.
